title: Cross-SDK Embeddings/Rerank: ergonomic streaming + adaptive backoff helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver language-idiomatic helpers and example patterns for Embeddings + Rerank use cases across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that improve streaming ergonomics, add adaptive retry/backoff primitives, and expose pagination/batching helpers for large-result workflows.

Scope:
- Ergonomic streaming helper wrappers that unify chunked embedding ingestion and rerank streaming results semantics across SDKs (async generators in Python, AsyncIterator in TS, channel-based iterator in Go).
- Adaptive backoff and retry middleware tuned for embeddings/rerank: retries for transient 429/5xx with jittered exponential backoff, token-aware retry limits (avoid repeating expensive long-context rerank), and optional idempotency keys.
- Pagination and batching utilities: cursor-based pagination iterator, token/size-aware batcher for embeddings uploads, and helpers to coalesce small requests into larger batches while respecting latency SLOs.
- Cross-language examples and runnable sandboxes demonstrating: streaming rerank results while concurrently uploading embeddings, graceful cancellation, and resume from pagination cursors.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API parity docs showing equivalent high-level primitives in Python/TS/Go with idiomatic names and patterns.
2) Unit and integration tests covering: retry/backoff behavior, streaming cancellation, pagination resume, and batch size heuristics.
3) Benchmarks demonstrating <=10% median latency regression for single-request paths and >=2x throughput improvement for batched embeddings ingestion compared to baseline.
4) Three example apps (one per language) in the repo under examples/embeddings-rerank demonstrating production patterns.

Non-goals: implementing new server-side endpoints, changing backend pagination contracts, or introducing new network protocols.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We prioritize developer ergonomics over a single API surface. Each SDK exposes a similar primitive but adapts to language idioms (e.g., async generator vs AsyncIterator vs channel). This increases maintenance but reduces cognitive friction for users.
- Adaptive backoff leverages per-request metadata (expected token count). We decided not to auto-rewrite prompt payloads to smaller sizes inside SDKs to avoid unexpected model quality changes.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/124567/embeddings-rerank-sdk-helpers
Example sandboxes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/main/embeddings-rerank
Benchmark dashboard: https://internal.redwood.com/dashboards/sdk-benchmarks/embeddings-rerank

2026-02-22 - Design feedback (Maya Gonzales): Prefer language-idiomatic iterator names: Python: stream_rerank(), TS: createRerankStream(), Go: RerankStream(ctx). Also requested a visual sequence diagram in the design doc.

2026-02-25 - Engineering notes (Liam Chen): Implemented Python async generator and TS AsyncIterator prototype. Initial Go channel-based prototype. Added adaptive backoff middleware with tunable parameters. Filed PR #4221 for Python changes.

2026-03-02 - Benchmarks (SRE): Baseline comparison run: batched embeddings ingestion shows 2.6x throughput at 95th percentile under synthetic workload (batch size 128). Single-request median latency increased by 6% due to additional middleware; acceptable per SLOs.

2026-03-05 - Code review (Jared Kim): Requested clearer docs around idempotency keys and that retries should be disabled by default for rerank when user supplies long contexts. Also noted missing unit tests for pagination cursor resume edge-case.

2026-03-09 - PR updates (Liam Chen): Addressed review comments, added tests for cursor resume, added flag `retry_on_long_context` with default false, and added TypeScript examples for cancellation behavior. Opened unified PRs: GH #4287 (TS), GH #4289 (Go).
2026-03-11 - QA (Nina Shah): Integration smoke tests passed in staging. Observability hooks added: per-request retry count and backoff time exposed to Console via trace attributes.
